text.p: These are the leading stories in Serbian and Montengrin press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- SERBIA --
POLITIKA
- Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic invited chairmen of parliamentary parties to discuss the working version of the draft law on local self-government.
- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic and visiting Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Igor Ivanov underlined the importance of strenghtening relations and intensifying cooperation.
- Yugoslav and Mexican parliamentarians discuss resumption of bilateral cooperation.

- Economic potential of Yugoslavia is very good and Great Britain will have important role in future economic cooperation of the two countries, said David Slinn, first secretary in the British embassy to Belgrade.
- The final version of the bill on ownership transformation in June. Company shares also for farmers and foreign currency depositors -- another step towards new rules for privatisation in Serbia.

- Yugoslavia has sown 55,800 hectares under sugar beet, or 56 percent of the plan, but down 20 percent compared to 1996. The country could produce 170,000-200,000 tonnes of sugar this year. Current reserves are between 60,000-80,000 tonnes and annual needs stand at 200,000 tonnes of sugar due to low standard of living.
- According to the federal statistics office average Yugoslav wage in April stood at 733 dinars.
- Serbian Education Minister Jovo Todorovic said teachers will soon get their wages.
- Health workers' strike continues. Only emergency cases are treated.
NASA BORBA
- Eighth day of health and social workers' strike. Talks with the government unsuccesful.

- Russia's Deputy Foreign Minister Igor Ivanov says after meeting Milosevic that Yugoslavia must reintegrate into international institutions; tells the Serbian opposition they can count on democratic elections.
- The U.N. General Secretary Koffi Annan supports the work of the Centre for democracy in the Balkans and says hopes for progress on the Balkans, especially in Bosnia.
- Status of Kosovo depends on the U.S. and internal political events in Yugoslavia and Albania, says Stipe Suvar, former Croatian communist leader in old Blkan federation.
- The ruling Socialist Party of Serbia is secretly preparing a new election law to introduce proportional system and a five percent census into the local elections.

- Battle for presidency nominations begins in Montenegro; according to some speculations, republic's Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic will run as independent presidential candidate if the ruling Democratic Party of Socialists fails to nominate him.

- The Serbian government's team of experts to go public with a draft privatisation law in ten days, abandoning the idea to make the privatisation compulsory and redifining the position of the share fund. Farmers will be included.
- Trade unions of the Serbian PTT accuse the republic's government of preparing a major sell-off of the company and intending to put the money on their private accounts.
- Special federal government comission prepared a bill on old foreign currency savings; term for final payments from five to 13 years.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Some 1.2 million pensioners to receive on Tuesday second half of their February pensions, 19 days after first half was paid out. The average amount to be paid out is 388 dinars.
- Serbian minister for education Jovo Todorovic said teachers' will be payed out by Friday.
-- MONTENEGRO --
POBJEDA

- The Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) local branch of Berane nominated republic's President Momir Bulatovic for presidental elections who said the north of the republic was neglected and announced struggle against grey economy.
- DPS local branch of Niksic proposed prime minister Milo Djukanovic and parliament speaker Svetozar Marovic as presidental candidates.
- Republics interior minister Filip Vujanovic opened new police offices in Pljevlja and said there were 325 criminal actds in 1996 in the town or 10.47 percent less than in the previous year.
- Montengro faces electric power deficit of 223 million kilowatt hours in the next five months.
- Montenegring health workers' trade unions support general strike of their Serbian colleagues.
- Montenegrin parliament resumes its session on Tuesday. -- Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 222 4254
